A standalone standard-library verifier passed 951 exact-algebra and numerical checks. Finite testing is not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2014 arXiv source proves general homogeneous-space mean-distance inequalities and does not give these distributions. The 2020 arXiv full text derives every three-dimensional homogeneous lens-space distance law but fixes complex dimension two; no theorem there covers the proposed higher-dimensional beta exponent and exact endpoint polynomial. Public literature and published mathematical research-record searches for the exact law, alternate cyclic-quotient description, geodesic-ball volumes and diameter-tail exponents returned no covering higher-dimensional theorem. This is a bounded best-evidence assessment, not conclusive historical priority. Full exact domain is complex dimension at least three.
residual_risks: Older or differently indexed all-dimensional lens-space geodesic ball formulas, including versions in Hopf-fibration coordinates, could exist; search is not historical priority proof.

value.rationale: A complete natural geometric probability invariant, the geodesic-ball volume distribution, is determined for every homogeneous scalar cyclic quotient of all odd spheres of dimension at least five. The exact polynomial of diameter-tail masses and the sharp jump from linear to quadratic decay at group order two distinguish inequivalent quotient geometries; strict order in both dimension and group order is a structural full-distribution comparison stronger than earlier mean-distance inequalities. The result is not a narrow parameter slice or mere recomputation of the already-known three-dimensional CDF.
